subject: CedarBridge HIPAA capabilities + PHI dataflow questions
content:
From: Alicia Reynolds <alicia.reynolds@cedarbridge.org>

Cc: procurement@cedarbridge.org
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HIPAA questionnaire follow-up + dataflow clarification

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — CedarBridge is evaluating vendor options for our new patient messaging feature. Our security team had a few follow-ups on PHI handling and a short set of questions attached to the RFP. Can you confirm:

- Where (in which components) PHI is encrypted at rest and in transit?
- Whether Redwood performs any persistent logging of full prompt/response content and whether that is toggleable per account.
- A simplified dataflow diagram showing how request traffic from our app would flow to Redwood and what elements might retain KV cache or logs.

We'd prefer short answers and a 30–45 minute technical call if needed. I attached the RFP excerpt.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Reynolds
Sourcing Manager, CedarBridge Health

-----Original Message-----
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com

Alicia — thanks for the clear list. See inline answers below and attached a concise dataflow PDF and our HIPAA capabilities summary. Happy to jump on a call with Monica (security) and Marcus (legal) if you want to walk through the diagram.

From: Alicia Reynolds <alicia.reynolds@cedarbridge.org>
> Where (in which components) PHI is encrypted at rest and in transit?

Response: All network traffic between CedarBridge and Redwood is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2+, and we support mutual TLS for Private deployments where required. PHI at rest is encrypted using customer-specific keys where customers use Redwood Private + KMS integration. For hosted Redwood API, data at rest is encrypted using AES-256; for customers requiring KMS/HSM-backed keys we support Bring-Your-Own-Key integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments.

From: Alicia Reynolds <alicia.reynolds@cedarbridge.org>
> Whether Redwood performs any persistent logging of full prompt/response content and whether that is toggleable per account.

Response: By default, Redwood collects request metadata and short-term logs for observability (latency/cost/trace ids). Persistent storage of full prompt/response pairs is off by default for enterprise accounts and is a configurable option. For customers on Dedicated or Private plans, persistent logging of content can be disabled entirely. For Hosted API customers, we offer configurable retention windows and an opt-out for content retention; these controls are exposed via Console and as part of the onboarding settings.

From: Alicia Reynolds <alicia.reynolds@cedarbridge.org>
> A simplified dataflow diagram showing how request traffic from our app would flow to Redwood and what elements might retain KV cache or logs.

Response: Attached: redwood-phi-dataflow-diagram.pdf with callouts. Short summary: requests hit our regional routing layer -> auth & customer routing -> serving runtime. KV cache is kept in-memory per GPU/serving node for latency; cache contents are not persisted to disk unless you enable persistent caching (opt-in). Audit/event logs (metadata) are written to encrypted object storage with configurable retention; full content logging is separately configurable as noted above.

Call: we're available Wed 12th 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 13th 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@cedarbridge.org>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HIPAA questionnaire follow-up + dataflow clarification

Michael — quick technical follow-up:

- KV cache is in-memory only by default. Each serving node keeps per-request KV fragments in DRAM; we do not swap or write decrypted model context to disk under normal operation.
- For workloads that enable persistent caching for cold-start optimization, those caches are encrypted at rest and stored in customer-scoped encrypted object storage; enabling persistent caching is an explicit configuration and reviewed during onboarding.
- No background process indexes or stores plaintext prompt/response content unless content logging is enabled by the customer or Redwood is operating under a Dedicated/Private setup with logging configured.

If helpful, I can provide a short appendix with service configuration flags and CLI values for persistent cache and retention durations.

Regards,
Monica Patel
